correctness.rationale: On each matched pair, knowing whether is equality of the two membership bits. At a site their conjunction is unanimity of the two neighboring bits and the center, including coincident neighbors when m=1. Applying it twice gives the stated five-bit test. Each indexed cyclic word satisfying the test has one based closed walk of its length in the four-bit overlap graph, and overlapping vertices recover the indexed word, even for lengths below five. An independent graph check gives an isolated 1111 loop, one eight-vertex cyclic component, and seven acyclic vertices. In the eight-vertex component every cycle passes through 1000: one can go from 1000 to 0001 directly or through 0000, then return through either 0010,0100 or 0011,0110,1100. This gives first-return lengths 4,5,5,6 and determinant det(I−sM)=(1−s)(1−s^4−2s^5−s^6). Factoring its degree-six part in the eigenvalue variable gives (z³−z−1)(z³+z+1); the characteristic polynomial also has z^9 from zero eigenvalues. Hence traces of positive powers give the claimed count at n=2m. Any one-bit equal to one in a fixed word forces both neighbors to be one, and the all-zero word maps to all ones. The unique fixed event leaves all other period-dividing-two events in pairs. Separately the matrix and direct local-rule enumeration at n=2,4,…,16 reproduced the characteristic polynomial and the eight counts; the supplied checker was inspected but not run. The finite census is corroboration, unlike the all-length walk argument.
